conclusion.justification: The report explicitly confirms the claim, stating that the evidence strongly supports that Kyleena is FDA-approved for pregnancy prevention for up to five years based on official prescribing labels and clinical trial data.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
The claim is accurate, not false.

Multiple independent, authoritative sources confirm that the FDA approved Kyleena (levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system, 19.5 mg) specifically for pregnancy prevention for up to five years. The official FDA-approved prescribing label states directly: "Kyleena is indicated to prevent pregnancy for up to 5 years," and further instructs that "Kyleena should not remain in the uterus after 5 years" and should be replaced after five years if continued use is desired (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2016/208224s000lbl.pdf; https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=2e07c155-21e1-4781-9633-ce8bddd47080).

This is corroborated by Bayer's own FDA approval announcement, which states the FDA "approved Kyleena™ (levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system) 19.5 mg… for the prevention of pregnancy for up to five years" (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/fda-approves-bayers-kyleena-levonorgestrel-releasing-intrauterine-system-195-mg-for-prevention-of-pregnancy-for-up-to-five-years-300330006.html).

Additionally, the FDA's own summary review of the New Drug Application (NDA 208224) describes the Phase III clinical trial data—based on the Pearl Index, the standard contraceptive efficacy measure—that supported this five-year approval (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/208224Orig1s000SumR.pdf).

**Conclusion:** The evidence strongly supports the claim as true. Kyleena is indeed FDA-approved for contraception for up to five years, based on Phase III clinical trial data and documented in the official FDA label and approval announcement. There is no credible evidence in the search results contradicting this; the user's skepticism about the claim being "false" is not supported by the retrieved evidence.
